attributes.body:
HappyRobot closes $150 million funding round.

Bankinter, through its Venture Capital division, has participated in HappyRobot's $150 million Series C funding round. The company specializes in AI agents for automating complex business operations. The transaction was led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo, and forms part of the bank's commitment to investing in highly innovative companies.

Existing investors a16z, Base10 and Y Combinator are reinforcing their investment alongside strategic partners including, in addition to Bankinter, Koch Disruptive Technologies (KDT), Kfund, Orange, T.Capital (Deutsche Telekom), Endeavor Catalyst, and Wave-X.

The round values the company at $1.2 billion post-money, bringing total funding to approximately $200 million and marking a new stage of growth as companies deploy AI agents across business-critical processes.

HappyRobot focuses on developing business superintelligence. Its platform enables organizations to create, deploy, and manage AI agents that automate complex operational workflows across voice, email, documents and the web. By learning from every interaction and execution, HappyRobot helps organizations capture operational knowledge, optimize information sharing and gain real-time visibility into their operations.

HappyRobot currently works with more than 150 large enterprises, including DHL, Kuehne + Nagel, Naturgy, Repso,l and Uber, and has grown fivefold since closing its Series B round at the end of last year.

After establishing its platform in the logistics sector - one of the world's most complex operating environments - the company is expanding into sectors such as insurance, energy and utilities, telecommunications, airlines, and other industries, where a significant share of operations still relies on manual processes and fragmented systems.

The new capital injection will enable HappyRobot to accelerate the development of its platform, expanding its AI capabilities, integrations with enterprise systems and the infrastructure required to deploy AI agents at scale. The company will also strengthen its global engineering, implementation, and business development teams to meet growing demand from companies across different sectors.

About HappyRobot.

The company was co-founded by Pablo Palafox, Javier Palafox, and Luis Paarup, who serve as CEO, COO, and CTO, respectively. Over the past year, the HappyRobot has expanded from two offices to eight locations across North America, Europe, Latin America, and Australia, reflecting growing demand from companies seeking to automate complex operational workflows.

Photo: From left to right: Luis Paarup, Javier Palafox and Pablo Palafox
attributes.title: HappyRobot closes $150 million funding round.

attributes.body:
Happyrobot Inc. has raised $150 million in Series C funding to build Enterprise Superintelligence.

New funding led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo will accelerate its global growth as Happyrobot Inc. expand its engineering, deployment and go-to-market teams

Kathryn Dean

Happyrobot Inc. is excited to share that Happyrobot Inc. has raised $150 million in Series C funding, led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo. Existing investors a16z, Base10, and Y Combinator are doubling down, joined by strategics including Koch Disruptive Technologies (KDT), Kfund, Orange, T.Capital (Deutsche Telekom), Bankinter, Endeavor Catalyst, and Wave-X.

This round values Happyrobot Inc. at $1.2 billion post-money, bringing its total funding to around $200 million as Happyrobot Inc. enter a new stage of growth, deploying its AI agents across more of the mission-critical work enterprises can't afford to get wrong.

The real economy, at scale.

Happyrobot Inc. now work with more than 150 enterprise customers, including DHL, Kuehne + Nagel, Naturgy, Repsol, and Uber, and Happyrobot Inc. has grown 5x since raising its Series B late last year. After first proving its platform in logistics, one of the world's most operationally demanding industries, Happyrobot Inc. is expanding across the supply chain as well as into insurance, energy and utilities, telecommunications, airlines, and other sectors where business-critical work still depends on manual coordination across fragmented systems.

Why Happyrobot Inc. is raising.

This new funding will accelerate investment in its platform, including expanded AI capabilities, enterprise integrations, and the infrastructure required to deploy AI agents at scale. Happyrobot Inc.'ll also continue growing its engineering, deployment, and go-to-market teams globally to support increasing demand from enterprises across industries.

"Getting agents to do work is the starting point, not the destination," said Pablo Palafox, its co-founder and CEO. "Our thesis is that enterprise superintelligence, where an organization's collective intelligence compounds as agents and people learn from one another, requires far more than task-performing agents. It requires a platform and a deployed motion capable of operationalizing that platform inside a specific business."

The numbers behind the platform.

Enterprise operations continue to rely on millions of phone calls, emails, documents, and disconnected systems every day. While AI has made it easier to generate information, many organizations still struggle to automate the work required to keep their businesses running. Happyrobot Inc. bridge that gap by deploying AI agents that can execute and reason within existing enterprise systems while working alongside employees.

Through the millions of tasks its agents execute each month, its customers are seeing measurable impact across departments. Deployment isn't a one-time project for Happyrobot Inc. but an ongoing partnership: initial agents typically go live within 4 to 12 weeks, and each sprint that follows refines the agents already in production and adds new ones. One of its customers is automating 28,000 hours of work every month. In customer care, its agents are achieving 9.4/10 customer satisfaction scores and more than 70% autonomous resolution on average. Its customers' operational teams have increased capacity by 10x, and their sales teams have generated 5x more revenue through previously underutilized channels.

Investor perspectives.

"Many industries have a surprising share of their costs locked up in coordination, the calls, emails, and handoffs that keep work flowing," said Kerry Wei, Partner at Prysm Capital. "While getting an agent to complete a discrete task is increasingly simple, deploying them across multi-step enterprise workflows has proven far more difficult. HappyRobot has built the missing link - the governance, interfaces, and context layer - that enables agents to work seamlessly across complex workflows, driving real ROI by allowing companies to capture value without asking employees to adopt anything new. We were blown away by what Pablo and the team already have running in production, and by the boldness of their vision. We are thrilled to partner with the team we believe is positioned to redefine how enterprise operations get done."

"It had been a while since we met a company that fundamentally expands what enterprise AI can do," said Anne-Charlotte Philbert, Partner at Eurazeo. "While most AI enhances individual productivity, HappyRobot automates complex, end-to-end business operations with AI agents already running in production at scale. From day one, we knew Pablo and the team were building something special: a truly AI-native platform, world-class technical depth, and customers seeing exceptional ROI in mission-critical industries such as supply chain, energy, telecommunications, and banking. We're excited to partner with HappyRobot as they build the AI-native operating system for enterprise operations and accelerate their expansion across Europe."

Over the past year, Happyrobot Inc. has expanded from two offices to eight locations across North America, Europe, LATAM, and Australia, reflecting growing demand from enterprises looking to automate complex operational workflows.

Company news, Press releases

HappyRobot secures $44M in Series B funding to expand its AI operating system for logistics and industrial enterprises.

Enterprise AI strategy

The path to Enterprise Superintelligence starts with execution. AI agents learn from every workflow, building context no model can buy.

Series B announcement.

HappyRobot secures $44M in Series B funding to expand its AI operating system for logistics and industrial enterprises.

Carlos Becker

Deployment Lead

Happyrobot Inc. is excited to share some big news: HappyRobot has raised a $44 million Series B, led by Base10 Partners with participation from a16z, Array Ventures, Avra, Samsara Ventures, Tokio Marine, WaVe-X, WiL, YC, and other strategic investors.

This milestone comes just 10 months after its $15.6M Series A, bringing its total funding to $62 million.

From first customer to 70+ enterprises.

Just a year and a half ago, Happyrobot Inc. went into production with its very first customer. Today, Happyrobot Inc. is proud to be powering operations for more than 70 enterprise customers, including DHL, Ryder, Schneider, and Werner.

These companies are already seeing what's possible when AI workers step in to take on complex, high-volume tasks:

* Appointment scheduling reduced from a week to under 30 minutes
* Collections delivering returns of more than 100x
* Outbound sales producing ROI north of 19x
* Carrier sales driving 5x returns

The early results are clear: AI workers aren't just cutting costs - they're unlocking new revenue opportunities, increasing visibility, and freeing teams to focus on strategic, relationship-driven work.

Building the AI operating system for the real economy.

Its mission is ambitious: to build the AI operating system for the real economy.

The AI OS is a system that closes the circuit between intelligence and action. By combining real-time truth, specialized AI workers, and an orchestrating intelligence, HappyRobot manages complex, mission-critical work with true autonomy. Starting with supply chain and industrial-scale operations, Happyrobot Inc. empower enterprises to operate with speed and continuous improvement - while humans focus on higher-value work.

This is just the beginning. Impact is exponential with an intelligence that learns & improves in real time.

Accelerating with Series B.

This new round of funding will help Happyrobot Inc. accelerate towards its mission by

* Hiring world-class talent to join its team
* Continuing to advance the product and make its product even more powerful
* Expanding into more enterprise deployments

It's fuel to scale what Happyrobot Inc. has built so far - and to keep pushing toward the operating system that the world's most impactful companies will run on.

Happyrobot Inc. is just getting started.

Happyrobot Inc. is deeply grateful to its team, customers, partners, and investors who believe in this mission & support Happyrobot Inc. in getting there.

Happyrobot Inc. is hiring. If you want to help Happyrobot Inc. build the operating system that powers the real economy, come join Happyrobot Inc..

Series A announcement.

Happyrobot Inc. is excited to announce its $15.6M Series A round led by Andreesen Horowitz (a16z), with support from RyderVentures and other strategic investors.

Carlos Becker

Deployment Lead

Happyrobot Inc. is excited to announce its $15.6M Series A round led by Andreesen Horowitz (a16z), with support from RyderVentures and other strategic investors.

This brings its total amount raised to $17.5M, with previous seed funding from Array Ventures and Y Combinator, and supports its mission to automate communication across the supply chain.

Its why.

Happyrobot Inc. started this journey because of Javi's (Co-founder & COO) experience on the shipper side, paying fines to retailers for falling short on their OTIF scorecards. He knew the problem stemmed from communication gaps along the journey of the load.

Pablo (Co-founder & CEO) & Luis (Co-founder & CTO) had extensive experience in AI research and were eager to apply recent breakthroughs in voice AI technology.

With Javi's insights, and its understanding that phone calls are at the heart of communication in logistics, Happyrobot Inc. has a clear understanding of the problem & are passionate about solving it.

Communication in logistics quickly becomes overwhelming, especially when there aren't enough hands to pick up every phone call or stay on top of every load. Happyrobot Inc. is eager to tackle this challenge for an industry that's so critical to its global economy, a sentiment shared by its partners at a16z.

"Today, the logistics industry underpinning our global economy is stretched. As a key part of the ecosystem, even small to midsize freight brokers can make and receive hundreds, if not thousands, of calls per day - and hiring for this job is increasingly difficult," said Anish Acharya, general partner at a16z. "By providing customers with autonomous decision making, HappyRobot's agentic AI platform helps these brokers operate more reliably and efficiently."

Where Happyrobot Inc. is today.

It's been a year since Happyrobot Inc. started building HappyRobot, and Happyrobot Inc. is now working with over 50 customers, automating millions of phone calls.

Its platform deploys AI agents - what Happyrobot Inc. like to call AI workers - that can handle conversations and take action on their own. Unlike the more rigid RPA systems of the past, its AI workers are dynamic, reacting to conversations as they unfold while always keeping the end goal in mind.

Its AI workers fully integrate with existing systems and do more than just read information - they log offers, load details, and critical updates. Everything is recorded and can be leveraged for future use.

Starting with the complex communication needs of freight brokers, its AI workers are often automating inbound and outbound carrier sales, various check calls, and POD collections. Today, Happyrobot Inc. is helping brokers, carriers, freight forwarders, warehouses, and others across the supply chain boost efficiency, improve margins, and free up human teams from repetitive tasks, allowing them to focus on more strategic work.

Its customers are seeing tremendous value in implementing HappyRobot, reducing call times by half and cutting operational costs by a third. "By August, we'd completed over 100,000 AI-driven calls using HappyRobot and expect to do ten times that amount next year," said Andrew Smith, SVP at Circle Logistics. "Using HappyRobot's agentic AI, 100% of calls were answered 24/7 with no hold time and our staff are using phones to do higher value work like build relationships rather than just to exchange data."

What's next.

Happyrobot Inc. is still all in on the supply chain. While there are plenty of general voice AI applications out there, Happyrobot Inc. believe the real impact comes from applying AI to specific industries. The supply chain, in particular, has so many unique details in every conversation that broad, general-purpose AI tools just don't address. Happyrobot Inc. is focused on getting those nuances right to make a real difference.

Happyrobot Inc. is continuing to expand into additional communication platforms, including email and messaging, and Happyrobot Inc. has got a new platform launching soon. This one takes things up a notch with more complex workflows - its AI can even put people on hold while sending messages or making other calls. Plus, it remembers past conversations, providing more context to personalize calls.

Happyrobot Inc.'ll be using the funds from this round to continue supporting its incredible customers and partners by bringing on talented people to join its team. Happyrobot Inc. is on the lookout for folks who can help Happyrobot Inc. build best in class technology while delivering excellent service.

Grateful for another day building the future with the best team in the game. Now, back to work!!!

Enterprise AI strategy

Its manifesto is the belief that true transformation begins when machines don't just analyze, but act.

NTT DOCOMO Ventures invests in HappyRobot, a u.s.-based innovator in AI Worker platforms.

NTT DOCOMO Ventures is pleased to announce that, through a fund that it manages, it has invested in HappyRobot, a company providing a platform for AI Workers.

The HappyRobot AI Worker Platform

HappyRobot offers a platform that builds and operates "AI Workers" capable of autonomously performing a wide range of tasks such as phone calls, emails, chat, and document processing. With this capability, enterprises can delegate repetitive tasks including call center operations and document handling to AI, enabling significant cost reductions and improved operational efficiency.

Unlike single-function automation, the HappyRobot AI Workers feature long-term contextual memory, compounding intelligence, and strong integration with existing systems, delivering proven results across diverse business domains. Their adoption is already expanding among major global enterprises, where outcomes such as increasing operational velocity from months to hours have been observed. For example, HappyRobot has reported achieving a 19x return on investment in outbound sales calls using its AI Workers.

Amid the global trend of leveraging AI to improve operational efficiency and address labor shortages, the HappyRobot AI Workers are positioned not merely as tools to supplement human tasks, but as autonomous entities capable of carrying out work without presupposing human involvement. This transformative approach has the potential to fundamentally change the way businesses operate. As a next-generation platform company driving automation through AI, HappyRobot is expected to achieve further growth in the years ahead.

NTT DOCOMO Group aims to drive innovation across society and industry by supporting digital transformation (DX) for enterprises, thereby contributing to the future of local communities and economies. Through this investment in HappyRobot, a company tackling the automation of white-collar work with AI, we will deepen our collaboration and advance initiatives to create new value.

HappyRobot is an enterprise-grade platform to build, deploy, and manage an AI workforce. They work with supply chain enterprises to automate end-to-end tasks at scale, leveraging communication, document parsing, web browsing, and other models to offload complex tasks from human teams. HappyRobot enables enterprises to move faster, automate information exchange, and get real time data visibility across the organization. Common use cases include inbound and outbound sales, shipment updates, scheduling, payment collections, recruiting, and support, working across the organization as an AI partner. For more information, please visit www.happyrobot.ai.
